Hoshea
ho-SHE-uh
proper noun (figure)
Hebrew Hoshea (H1954) — "salvation" or "he has saved"; from yasha ("to save, deliver"). The same root produces both the Hebrew name and (with the Yah- prefix) the name Yehoshua — "Yahweh saves," rendered into Greek as Iēsous, "Jesus." Moses's original name for his successor Joshua was Hoshea (Num 13:8), which Moses then expanded to Joshua (Num 13:16).

📖 Biblical Definition

Hoshea (c. 732 — 722 BC) was the nineteenth and final king of the divided northern kingdom of Israel (2 Kings 17:1-23), assassin of his predecessor Pekah, vassal of the Assyrian kings Tiglath-Pileser III and Shalmaneser V, and the king during whose reign Samaria fell to Sargon II of Assyria in 722 BC and the ten northern tribes were carried into the captivity from which they never returned as a distinct people. His nine-year reign represents the slow strangulation of the northern kingdom by Assyrian power. The canonical verdict is striking: "And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him" (2 Kings 17:2) — the only Israelite king of whom the not-as-bad-as-his-predecessors qualifier is used. The Chronicler does not narrate his reign at all (he focuses entirely on the southern kingdom by this point). His name — "salvation" — is haunting: he was the final king and his name meant deliverance, but no deliverance came. He attempted to break free from Assyrian vassalage by appealing for help to So king of Egypt (probably Osorkon IV or possibly Tefnakht of Sais); Shalmaneser V detected the rebellion, imprisoned Hoshea, besieged Samaria for three years (725-722 BC), and finally took the city. The 27 verses of 2 Kings 17:7-23 constitute the most sustained Old Testament theological retrospective on why the northern kingdom fell: idolatry from the days of Jeroboam I, refusal of prophetic warning, golden calves at Bethel and Dan, high places, asherah-poles, child-sacrifice, Baal-worship, divination, and ultimately exile. The chapter is essential reading for understanding the structure of covenant judgment in the divided monarchy.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Nineteenth and final king of the northern kingdom of Israel (c. 732-722 BC); vassal of Assyria; rebelled by appealing to Egypt; Samaria fell to Sargon II in 722 BC and the ten tribes were carried into exile; called 'evil but not as the kings of Israel before him' (2 Kings 17:2).

HOSHEA, proper noun. Hebrew Hoshea (H1954) — "salvation," from yasha ("to save"). Same root as Joshua (Yehoshua, "Yahweh saves") and ultimately Jesus.

Nineteenth and final king of the divided northern kingdom of Israel (c. 732-722 BC); assassinated Pekah to take the throne (2 Kings 15:30).

Vassal of Tiglath-Pileser III and Shalmaneser V; rebelled by appealing to So king of Egypt; imprisoned by Shalmaneser; Samaria besieged 725-722 BC.

Samaria fell to Sargon II of Assyria in 722 BC; the ten northern tribes carried into Assyrian exile.

Distinct from Hosea the prophet (same Hebrew name but different person; Hos 1:1).

📖 Key Scripture

2 Kings 17:2-4 — "And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him. Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents. And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year: therefore the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison."

2 Kings 17:6 — "In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes."

2 Kings 17:18 — "Therefore the LORD was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only."

Hosea 13:16 — "Samaria shall become desolate; for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shall be dashed in pieces, and their women with child shall be ripped up."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Hoshea is corrupted when the 'evil but not as the kings before him' qualifier is read as partial vindication rather than as the bitter Chronicler-irony it actually is, when his fall is treated as merely the outcome of geopolitical pressure rather than as covenant judgment, or when the 27-verse theological retrospective of 2 Kings 17:7-23 is skipped in favor of the narrative chapters around it.

expand to see more

Not-as-bad qualifier misread. 2 Kings 17:2's phrase 'he did evil... but not as the kings of Israel that were before him' has sometimes been read as partial vindication of Hoshea — the least-bad of a bad lot. The narrative immediately undercuts this: Hoshea's nine-year reign ended in the fall of Samaria, the destruction of the northern kingdom, and the deportation of the ten tribes. The not-as-bad-as-Ahab qualifier is a bitter Chronicler-irony, not a vindication. Even diminished apostasy in the final king did not avert the long-prepared judgment that the earlier kings had earned.

Geopolitical-pressure determinism. Modern Near-Eastern-history readings of 722 BC sometimes treat the fall of Samaria as the predictable outcome of Assyrian military superiority and Israelite geopolitical miscalculation (appealing to Egypt against the wrong superpower). 2 Kings 17:7-23 explicitly rejects this reading. The 27-verse theological retrospective gives the cause as covenant breach, not military weakness: 'For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God... and walked in the statutes of the heathen... and the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the LORD their God... and they served idols, whereof the LORD had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing' (verses 7-12). Geopolitics was the instrument; covenant judgment was the cause.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Hoshea (H1954) — "salvation," from yasha ("to save"). Same root as Joshua and Jesus. Nineteenth and final king of the divided northern kingdom (c. 732-722 BC); deposed when Samaria fell to Sargon II.

Hebrew Hoshea (H1954) — "salvation" or "he has saved"

From the root yasha — "to save, deliver"

Same root as Yehoshua (Joshua, "Yahweh saves") and ultimately Greek Iēsous (Jesus)

Usage
